'''Atorada''' or '''Atoraí''' is a moribund [[Arawakan language]] of [[Brazil]] and [[Guyana]]. There were only a few speakers as of 2000. The language is poorly documented, and it is frequently seen as a dialect of closely related [[Wapishana language|Wapishana]].

== History ==
The [[Atorai people]] and language were historically distributed between the [[Rupununi]] and [[Kuyuwini River|Kuyuwini Rivers]], but later migrated among the [[Wapishana]] people, when they began to switch to the Wapishana language. [[William Curtis Farabee|William Farabee]] (1918) reported the customs of the Atorai to be essentially identical with those of the Wapishana.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Farabee |first=William C. |url=https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/biblio%3Afarabee-1918-arawaks/Farabee_1918_TheCentralArawaks_BDCN.pdf |title=The Central Arawaks |date=1918 |publisher=University Museum |series=University Museum Anthropological Publication |volume=IX |location=Philadephia}}</ref> The only significant documentation of Atorai are two wordlists in [[Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius]]'s 1867 work ''Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium'' and another recorded by Farabee and published in 1918, as well as a talk held in 2018 by Zachary O'Hagan.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Citation |last=Miller |first=Zaphiel K. |title=Phylogenetic Classification of the Negro-Roraima Subgroup |date=2021 |work= |pages=16–29, 52–56 |url=https://berkeley.app.box.com/s/wf0tcv1tl6ugs2vqlakix5vp3q9uy0qm |access-date=2026-05-03 |chapter=Atorai Phonology |place=Berkeley |publisher=University of California at Berkeley}}</ref>

Voice is not contrasted for [[Obstruent|obstruents]], and instead of voiced stops, voiced [[Implosive consonant|implosives]] occur in Atorai.<ref name=":1" />{{rp|page=18}}

=== Phonotactics ===
Atorai has a (C)V(V)(C) syllable structure. The glottal stop cannot occur word-initially.<ref name=":1" />{{rp|page=|pages=26–27}}
